title: Privileged roles cleanup sprint and audit evidence pipeline notes
body:
Overview:

This is a working note for the privileged-roles cleanup sprint (iteration 2026-Q4 sprint 1) and the related audit-evidence pipeline we need to land for the upcoming quarterly access review. The doc captures goals, acceptance criteria, mapping between RBAC v2 role constructs and audit log fields, SIEM export considerations, and a short implementation backlog for automation.

High-level goals (Sprint scope):
- Remove stale privileged roles and merge near-duplicate role grants in IAM console and RBAC v2 config.
- Ensure every privileged role has an evidence template (how it was granted, justification, last use).
- Ship automated evidence export that collects required fields from the audit logs and pushes to the SIEM export topic and archive bucket.
- Validate that evidence artifacts satisfy the quarterly least-privilege recertification checklist used by compliance.

Why this matters now:
- Recent spot-checks found ~18 roles with overlapping scopes (create/update/delete + broad resource globs). Cleanups reduce blast radius and simplify future attestation.
- RBAC v2 landed last quarter but we still have legacy grants represented only in cloud IAM and in-house role-maps; need canonicalization for auditable recertification.

Primary stakeholders:
- Security & Compliance (owning recertification policy): Ava Martinez, Lina Gomez
- Identity/Platform team (owners of RBAC v2): Ravi Patel, Nick Howard
- Infra/SRE (audit log + SIEM pipeline): Ethan Cho, SRE Team
- Product/Platform owners for services with privileged roles (several service leads; we will tag them with PRs)

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
1) A documented list of privileged roles targeted for deletion/merge with owners and proposed action (delete/merge/reduce-scope).
2) For each targeted role, produce an evidence bundle containing: role definition, grant event(s) (audit log slice), last-activity timestamp, linked ticket/PR that requested the grant, approver identity.
3) A working automation pipeline: given a list of role IDs, it can export evidence bundles to S3-compatible archive and send a SIEM event (with standardized schema) to the compliance topic.
4) CI checks that verify exported evidence contains the mandatory schema fields (see 'Audit schema' below).

RBAC v2 mapping notes (practical):
- Role object canonical fields we rely on: role_id, role_name, description, scope_set (list of resource globs), permissions (list), created_by (principal), created_at, last_modified_at, active_principals (list)
- For legacy grants (cloud IAM bindings) we use a translation table: cloud_binding -> rbac_grant with a generated role_id and source_reference pointing back to the cloud binding resource URL.
- All role changes MUST have a corresponding change-event logged via our audit-log service (audit.v1.role.change). If missing, flag for manual review.

Audit log schema (required export fields):
(we will publish this as JSON schema in Confluence, but tests expect these fields in string form)
- event_id (string)
- event_type (string) e.g. "role.grant", "role.revoke", "role.change", "access.request"
- timestamp (ISO8601 string)
- actor_principal (string) // who performed the action
- target_role_id (string)
- target_role_snapshot (string) // base64-encoded JSON blob of role after change (or URL to snapshot)
- justification (string) // free text if provided during approval flow
- ticket_id (string) // link to JIRA/PR/confluence if referenced
- request_context (string) // e.g., IP, region, request_origin
- audit_source (string) // i.e. identity-service, cloud-iam-sync, rbac-v2-service
- proof_materials (string) // url(s) to artifacts (approvals, emails, PR diffs)
- last_activity_ts (ISO8601 string) // most recent action by a principal using that role

Notes on schema design choices:
- We intentionally duplicate a role snapshot to make offline recertification possible (archived evidence should be sufficient to understand the role without hitting the live DB). The snapshot can be stored as an object URL or embedded as base64 in the audit entry.
- proof_materials are free-form but must be resolvable to stored artifacts in the evidence bucket.

SIEM export mapping and constraints:
- SIEM ingest expects newline-delimited JSON with flat fields; nested snapshots must be encoded (base64 or object URL).
- Field names must follow snake_case to align with current SIEM parsers: event_id, event_type, timestamp, actor_principal, target_role_id, role_snapshot_url, justification, ticket_id, request_context, audit_source, proof_urls, last_activity_ts
- Minimum retention tag on SIEM events: retention=7y (configurable per compliance requirements).
- We will send two event types for recertification: "evidence.bundle.generated" (when automation compiles the full bundle) and "recertification.prompt.sent" (when reviewer notifications are triggered).

Evidence pipeline design (rough):
1) Input: CSV list of target role ids (generated from the role cleanup plan).
2) For each role_id:
   - Query RBAC v2 service to fetch role snapshot and active principals.
   - Query audit-log service for all events where target_role_id == role_id OR event_type in ("role.grant", "role.revoke", "role.change") within last 36 months.
   - Generate a canonical evidence bundle: metadata.json (flattened), role_snapshot.json (full), log_slice.ndjson (events), proofs/ (links to PRs, approvals).
   - Push bundle to evidence-archive bucket: s3://compliance-evidence/recertification/2026-Q4/<role_id>/bundle-<timestamp>.zip
   - Emit SIEM event with bundle metadata and link to archive.

Automation backlog (tickets & owners):
- JIRA-SEC-8421: create evidence exporter lambda + batch runner (owner: Ethan Cho)
- JIRA-SEC-8422: schema validation tests and contract for SIEM team (owner: Ravi Patel)
- JIRA-SEC-8423: role-canonicalization script (owner: Nick Howard)
- JIRA-SEC-8424: recertification email workflow integration (owner: Lina Gomez)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR#876 - initial exporter prototype (linked)

Quick checklist for reviewers (manual fallback):
- Does the evidence bundle contain a role_snapshot and at least one change event?
- Are access justifications present for grants older than 12 months?
- Is last_activity_ts accurate and within 30 days of the audit log?
- Are proof URLs resolvable and stored in the evidence-archive?

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Snapshot encoding: base64 blob in SIEM event vs object URL. Tradeoffs: URL reduces SIEM payload size but requires S3 auth to review; base64 is self-contained but large. Proposal: use URL in SIEM, embed base64 in the archived bundle. (PREFERRED)
- Retention window for events to include in bundle. Compliance asked for 36 months; platform team prefers 12 months for performance. Need sign-off.
- Auto-deprovision workflow for roles that are unused for >= 90 days but still granted. Should we auto-flag or auto-revoke? Recommend flag-only for now.

Next steps (this week):
- 2026-10-04: kickoff meeting with infra + identity to align on exporter approach (owners: Ethan, Ravi).
- 2026-10-06: land schema PR for audit export in confluence and repo (owner: Ravi).
- 2026-10-08: run a pilot on 10 roles (small set) to validate evidence bundles and SIEM events (owners: Nick, Ethan).

Meeting notes (9/30 ad-hoc):
- SRE raised concerns about scan frequency hitting the audit-log index; plan to use time-bounded queries and pagination.
- Identity team will publish a small helper endpoint to return role snapshots by id to avoid heavy joins.
- Compliance requires an approver identity in all evidence bundles; platform team must ensure UI/approval flow writes approver into justification field.

Appendix: example log_slice.ndjson (one-line-per-event)
{"event_id":"evt-0001","event_type":"role.grant","timestamp":"2024-11-20T15:23:10Z","actor_principal":"alice@redwood.com","target_role_id":"role-admin-analytics","justification":"oncall-access-for-analytics","ticket_id":"JIRA-1234","audit_source":"identity-service","last_activity_ts":"2026-09-10T12:00:00Z","proof_materials":"https://confluence.company/x/PR-567"}

Notes to self:
- Keep the sprint lightweight: focus on 20-40 high-risk roles first.
- Document the manual review playbook for the compliance team so they can accept bundles even if a few events are missing.

References:
- CONFLUENCE-1234-RBAC-V2-MAP (RBAC v2 canonical model)
- JIRA-SEC-8421 (exporter backlog)
- github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR#876 (prototype)

If you're reviewing: please add comments inline in this doc, or update the linked JIRA tickets. Will iterate after the kickoff.
